text: Habuit et Jonathan, Sauli filius, filium laesis pedibus, qui a nutrice annos quinque natus, audito quid Saulo et Jonathani apud Jezrael accidisset, sublatus, illa trepidantius fugiente, ceciderat, et claudus factus fuerat. Ei nomen erat Mephibosethus.
note: paragraph: the aside on Mephibosheth; 1738 indents here (text/orig/2SA.usfm) and the BSB breaks (b m); *Habuit* begins a sentence after 4:3's full stop (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: Hi Remmonis Berothitae filii Rechabus et Baana, feruente die, Isbosethi domum introgressi, qui tum in cubile meridiabatur,
note: paragraph: the murder of Ish-bosheth, the story resumed after the one-verse aside; the BSB breaks here (b m) and *Hī* begins a sentence after 4:4's full stop (1738 runs on from 4:4) (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: ad Davidem Hebronem attulerunt, regemque ita adlocuti sunt: “Ecce caput Isbosethi, Sauli filii, hostis tui, qui tibi necem moliebatur. Hodierno die Jova tibi, domine rex, supplicium de Saulo, deque ejus stirpe sumsit.”
note: the brothers' words direct (*ecce caput … sūmpsit*), after 1738's colon with no *inquit*, so the colon stays; capital at the speech's start; *domine rēx* lower case, addressed to David (as 1 Sam 1:15 *domine*); the draft's line break removed (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: At David Rechabo et Baanae fratribus in hunc modum respondit: “O Jova vivens, qui vitam meam ex omnibus periculis adservisti,
note: David's answer direct, 4:9–11 (the oath *Ō Jōva vīvēns*, *ego … comprehendī*, *nōn expetam?*), after 1738's colon; capital at the speech's start; the draft's line break removed; paragraph kept (the BSB's heading) (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: et a vobis hominibus impiis, qui hominem innocentem, domi suae, in suo cubili jugulastis, illius sanguinis poenas non expetam, vosque ex orbe terrarum auferam?”
note: David's speech closes at *auferam?*; the messenger's words inside 4:10 are reported (*Saūlī mortem … nūntiāvit*), no inner quotation where the BSB has one (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: quo duce (etiam antea regnante Saulo) usi fuerint Israelitae: Jovam ei sui populi Israelitici gubernationem destinasse: eumque imperium in Israelitas habiturum.

text: eoque die pronuntiavit David, quisquis Jebusaeos vicisset, et ad canalem pertigisset, claudosque et caecos Davidi invisos, ex quo natum est dictum illud: “Caecus et claudus domum ne intrent.”
note: the saying direct, as the proverbs of 1 Sam 10:12, 24:13 (*dictum illud:* then its words, *nē intrent*); capital at its start; David's proclamation before it (*quisquis … vīcisset … invīsōs*, a period left unfinished, as the Hebrew) and the Jebusites' taunt in 5:6 (*negantibus … irruptūrum esse*) are reported, unmarked where the BSB quotes (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: Misit autem ad eum Hiramus rex Tyri legatos, materiamque cedrinam, et fabros lignarios, lapidariosque ad parietes, qui ei domum construerent:
note: paragraph: Hiram's embassy and David's house; 1738 indents here and the BSB breaks (b m); the draft's paragraph at 5:12 moved here, since 5:12 *intellēxitque* continues this sentence after its colon (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: Tum David Jovam ita consuluit: “Adgrediarne Palaestinos? Eosne tu mihi in manum trades?” Cui Jova, “Adgredere,” inquit, “nam Palaestinos ego tibi in manum tradam.”
note: David's questions and God's answer direct (*adgrediarne*, *adgredere … trādam*); capital after the complete question (1738 lower case, its habit); where 1738 has *X: words, inquit:* the colon after the speaker is a comma and *inquit* is set off, the quotation closed and reopened (1 Sam 1:17, decision 65); the draft's line break removed (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: Tum David ad Baalpharasimum profectus, illos ibi vicit, atque ita dixit: “Fudit Jova hostes meos ad meum conspectum, sicuti funditur aqua.” Inde locus ille Baalpharasimum est nominatus,
note: David's words direct (*fūdit Jōva hostēs meōs*), after 1738's colon; capital at the speech's start; the draft's line break removed. God's second answer 5:23–24 is reported (*jussus est nōn adscendere … adīre … invādere … præitūrum esse*), unmarked where the BSB quotes (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: profectus est cum suis omnibus Judaicis copiis ad transferendam arcam divinam, in qua nomen, nomen Jovae armipotentis, Cherubis insidentis, invocabatur.
note: *Jūdaicīs* capital, an adjective of a people (as r1's 2:4 *Jūdaicī*; 1738 *iudaicis*) (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: Davide autem, totaque Israelitica stirpe, ludentibus ante Jovam, omne genus pineis instrumentis, et citharis, nablis, tympanis, tibiis et cymbalis.

text: Ubi ad Nachonis aream ventum est, Oza arcam, boum agitatione nutantem, admota manu sustentavit.
note: paragraph: Uzzah struck down; the BSB breaks here (b m, its heading at 6:5) and *Ubi* begins a sentence after 6:5's full stop (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: ubi in urbem Davidis ventum est, Michol Sauli filia per fenestram prospiciens, tripudiantem saltantemque coram Jova Davidem conspicata, eum in animo suo despexit.
note: no paragraph: the verse is the main clause of the sentence begun at 6:15 (*Ita cum arca … dūcerētur: ubi … ventum est, Mīchol … dēspexit*), and 1738 has no indent; Michal's scene gets its paragraph at 6:20, where 1738 indents (as Ruth 1:6) (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: Tum David ad fausta precandum domui suae se convertit: cui obviam progressa Michol Sauli filia, eum sic adloquitur: “O quanta fuit hodie regis Israelitarum gravitas? Qui se hodie, spectantibus suorum servorum ancillis, non aliter vulgaverit, quam se solent vulgare nebulones.”
note: paragraph: Michal and David; 1738 indents here and the BSB breaks (b m). Michal's words direct, after 1738's colon; capital at the speech's start and after the complete question (1738 *grauitas? qui*), *Quī* a connecting relative (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: Cui David, “Coram Jova,” inquit, “qui me tuo patri, totique ejus stirpi praepositum, jussit, suo Israelitico populo imperatorem esse, coram Jova, inquam, lusi,
note: David's answer direct, 6:21–22; the colon after *Cui Dāvīd* a comma before *inquit* (1 Sam 1:17), *inquit* set off with the quotation closed and reopened (decision 65); 1738's parenthesis *(quī mē … esse)*, which would open the resumed quotation, made commas; *inquam* inside the speech stays; *Isrāēlīticō* capital (1738 *israelitico*) (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: multoque magis me demittam, et meo judicio humilis, apud ancillas, de quibus tu locuta es, apud eas, inquam, gravis ero.”

text: Sed ea nocte Jova Nathanem sic adlocutus est:
note: paragraph: God's word to Nathan; the BSB breaks here (b m) and *Sed* begins a sentence after 7:3's full stop; 7:1–16 would be 269 words in one (decision 52): 42 and 227. David's proposal 7:2 and Nathan's answer 7:3 are reported (*absurdum esse*; *faceret sānē … Jōvam enim eī adesse*), unmarked where the BSB quotes (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: “I renuntiatum haec meo Davidi. Sic dicit Jova: ‘Tune mihi domum ad habitandum construes?
note: God's words to Nathan direct, 7:5–16, opened after 7:4's colon; the oracle Nathan is to carry in ‘…’ after *Sīc dīcit Jōva:*, the formula left outside the inner quotation as the settled 1 Sam 2:27, 10:18, 15:2 and Josh 24:2; capitals at each quotation's start (1738 *i renuntiatum*, *tune*) (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: Qui, ex quo Israelitas ex Aegypto eduxi, ad hunc diem, domum non habitavi, sed in tentorio atque tabernaculo versatus sum.
note: capital after the complete question (1738 *construes? qui*), *Quī* a connecting relative (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: Quamdiu inter omnes Israelitas versatus sum, ecquod ulli praesidum Israelitarum (cui meos Israelitas regendos mandaverim) verbum feci de construenda mihi domo cedrina?’
note: the oracle's first part closes here: 7:8 begins again with the formula *Quamobrem sīc dīcit Jōva armipotēns (dīcēs meō Dāvīdī)*, God speaking to Nathan (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: Quamobrem sic dicit Jova armipotens (dices meo Davidi): ‘Ego te a caula, a procuratione balantum, adscivi, ut mei Israelitici populi imperator esses:
note: the formula with God's aside to Nathan *(dīcēs meō Dāvīdī)* outside the inner quotation; a colon added after it to introduce the oracle, as *Sīc dīcit Jōva:* in 7:5 (1738 has none, but prints *Ego* with a capital); the oracle reopens in ‘…’; *Isrāēlīticī* capital (1738 *israelitici*) (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: tum ex quo tempore ego praesides meis Israelitis praeposui.’ Igitur tibi (inquies) ab omnibus hostibus tuis quieto reddito, nuntiat Jova, se domum esse instructurum.

text: ‘Quum plena aetate cum majoribus tuis obdormiveris, suscitabo prolem tuam post te, ex tuo ventre egressam, cujus regnum confirmabo.

text: tibique firma domus et regnum, et stabile solium permanebit in sempiternum.’”
note: God's words to Nathan close here, with the oracle inside them (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: Haec omnia verba, omneque oraculum, quum Nathan exposuisset Davidi,
note: paragraph: David's prayer; the draft's paragraph at 7:18 moved here, where Castellio's sentence begins (*Hæc omnia verba … cum Nāthan exposuisset Dāvīdī, īvit rēx*); the BSB breaks here (b m); 1738 has no indent in chapter 7 (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: ivit rex David ad Jovam, et apud eum ita locutus est: “Quis ego sum, o Domine Jova, aut quae mea stirps est, ut me hucusque adduxisse parum tibi visum fuerit, Domine Jova:
note: no paragraph: the verse is the main clause of the sentence begun at 7:17 (paragraph moved there). David's prayer direct, 7:18–29, after 1738's colon; capital at its start; *Domine* capital, God addressed by his title (1738 *Domine*); the draft's line break removed (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: Domine Jova, quid jam tibi David amplius dicet? Quum tu me tuum noveris, Domine Jova,
note: capital after the complete question (1738 *dicet? quum*); the *cum* clause goes with 7:21 *fēcistī* (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: “Ergo ita magnus es, Jova Deus, ut non solum nemo par tibi sit, sed ne Deus quidem sit ullus praeter te, ut quidem ipsi nostris auribus audivimus.
note: paragraph inside the prayer: 7:17–29 would be 285 words in one (decision 52): 105 and 180; the BSB breaks here (b m) and *Ergō* begins a sentence after 7:21's full stop; the quotation reopens at the new paragraph (1 Sam 2:31) (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: Ecquae omnino gens est cum tuis Israelitis in orbe terrarum conferenda? Quam dii redemtum iverint, ut eam pro sua haberent, ut ei famam conciliarent, ut ejus caussa tam inaudita et terribilia facerent, quam tu tuae terrae fecisti in tuorum gratiam,
note: capital after the complete question (1738 *conferenda? quam*), *Quam* a connecting relative (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: quos tibi ex Aegypti tum gentibus tum diis redemtos, sempiternum tibi populum Israeliticum stabilivisti: teque, Jova, ei Deum praebuisti.
note: *Isrāēlīticum* capital (1738 *israeliticum*) (reader r2, 2026-11-21)

text: Igitur age jam, perfice tuo favore, ut mea, qui tuus sum, propago per te perpetuo maneat. Nam tu, Domine Jova, promisisti futurum, ut mea propago tuo sit favore felix in sempiternum.”
note: David's prayer closes here; 1738's stray full stop inside the clause (*ut mea propago. tuo sit favore*, text/orig/2SA.usfm) dropped: a printer's slip, the *ut* clause running on to *fēlīx*; the draft's line break removed (reader r2, 2026-11-21)
